intro: Compare where movement, lighting and distortion come from in the frame.
alt: A softly outlined figure is followed by a skewed high-contrast cinema set and an office with hard striped shadow.

variants.name: rotoscope
variants.look: Naturalistic weight and posture survive inside the drawn outline.
variants.history: Max Fleischer patented a device for tracing sequential live-action frames, establishing an influential approach to rotoscoping.
variants.when: Use live-action motion as the basis for line, color and exaggeration.
variants.why: Traced position changes retain useful details about balance and timing.

variants.name: German Expressionist cinema
variants.look: Angular sets and slashed shadows make the whole scene look unsettled.
variants.history: German Expressionist cinema used distorted design and theatrical lighting to convey psychological conditions.
variants.when: Build fear or instability into the angles of the set itself.
variants.why: Sets with sloped geometry give psychological subjects a physical form.

variants.name: film noir
variants.look: Hard light through a blind cuts across a plausible office.
variants.history: The label film noir came to describe a cycle of American crime dramas and thrillers that often used low-key lighting, strong shadows and moral ambiguity.
variants.when: Use selective hard light to make an ordinary place feel uncertain.
variants.why: A convincing room made strange by selective light creates uncertainty while retaining a recognizable setting.
